recentItems.title: OCTOBER WILL BE EXPLOSIVE! Zelenskyy approves HARSH NEW STRIKES on Russia
recentItems.description:
Ukraine is intensifying long-range strikes on Russian oil facilities, drone depots, and logistics. Operation "Vivaldi" has halted the Russian advance toward Sloviansk and Kramatorsk: 176 km² have been reclaimed, over 5,000 occupiers killed or wounded, and around 250 captured. In this episode: preparation for the next stage of the operation, testing of interceptors for jet-powered "Shaheds," U.S. military aid, and conflicting signals from Germany regarding negotiations. How do rear strikes impact the front line and the Kremlin's oil revenues?

recentItems.title: Ukrainian Army liberates 176 km² and captures 250 POWs right under Kremlin's nose
recentItems.description:
A factory producing components for Russian missiles, three oil refineries, and six radars became targets of Ukrainian precision strikes. In this episode of Russian Losses, we calculate the true cost of the war for Russia: according to the General Staff, enemy casualties over the past week reached 11,890 troops killed and wounded. Meanwhile, the Kremlin plans to increase military spending and tax pressure, forcing Russian regions to cut healthcare budgets. Operation "Vivaldi" yielded 176 square kilometers of liberated territory and 250 captured Russian soldiers for Ukraine. How are deep strikes on production, fuel, and logistics impacting the Russian army? What will Russia run out of first — money or troops? Watch our breakdown and share your thoughts in the comments!

recentItems.title: 176 KM² ALREADY UNDER CONTROL! Robotic drones burn Russian rear, POWs in shock
recentItems.description:
Three Russian tanks were destroyed in a single sortie 65 km behind the frontline, while SOF operators captured occupiers directly in their rear. In this episode: Ukrainian drone operations, artillery hunting, and Russian war crimes involving the use of human shields. We discuss Operation "Vivaldi" — a defensive breakthrough, the liberation of 176 square kilometers, and the deployment of APCs repurposed as ground robotic systems. How did intelligence and strikes on enemy logistics ensure success? Why is NATO studying Ukrainian combat experience? We analyze Russian losses, the Kremlin’s plans to mobilize 300,000 troops, and the threat of hybrid attacks against Europe aimed at undermining support for Ukraine.

recentItems.title: Putin waves the peace flag while loading missiles: a farce no longer believed even by Trump
recentItems.description:
The Kremlin declares its readiness for negotiations, yet rejects cease-fire proposals. Why does Putin need a diplomatic farce, and what lies behind his talk of peace? According to The Kyiv Independent, citing sources, Donald Trump is skeptical about the chances of reaching an agreement with Putin to stop attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Moscow has made it clear that it is not prepared to accept the proposed deals. In this report, we analyze the contradiction between the Kremlin’s statements and actions, its response to Washington’s peace initiatives, and the threat of new strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. Watch the video for full details.

recentItems.title: EW is no longer saving them: Hornet drone burns occupiers' equipment 150 km behind the lines
recentItems.description:
The Ukrainian Hornet UAV strikes Russian military logistics up to 150 km behind the frontline. The Army Media team captured exclusive combat footage of the crew from the 25th Separate Airborne Sicheslav Brigade in action. Senior Lieutenant Yevheniy Nazarenko was shown an upgraded drone that utilizes Starlink instead of conventional radio relays.

Why did the occupiers initially nickname it "The Martian," and how does it operate under heavy Russian EW (electronic warfare)? Soldiers share insights into striking targets deep in enemy territory. Watch exclusive flight footage and a mission hunting down a Russian tank near Donetsk.
